title: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3: correct desegmentation of protocols inside streams
description:
Protocols encapsulated in the Extended HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 Connect treat data inside DATA frames as streams similar to TCP packets.
That is, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 DATA framing should be streamed and de-segmented by dissectors.
This MR does the following:
- extends existing HTTP/2 logic that is currently applied to GRPC to protocols inside Extended Connect (currently only websocket)
- implements similar HTTP/3 mechanism. Extended `reassemble_streaming_data_and_call_subdissector` to support QUIC `reassembly_table_functions`
- adjusts TCP `tcp_dissect_pdus` to deal with protocols that happen to be inside HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 streams rather than TCP

This MR corrects websockets desegmentation inside HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 and adds necessary building blocks for other protocols inside Extended Connect as well as future enablement of TCP dissectors for standard Connect in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

Can you provide a sample file to test against?

This looks like a wrong approach, and I oppose merging it in its current form.

I've put together a sample pcap with HTTP/3 and some test segmented websocket:

- packet 10 and 16 contains two websocket messages in a single DATA frame
- packets 11-12 and 17-18 contain one websocket message split across two DATA frames

[websocket-h3-segmented.pcapng](/uploads/d6238eefbecb18b8228ef7cbdfa6339c/websocket-h3-segmented.pcapng)

Modifying websocket dissector to call something instead of `tcp_dissect_pdus` when it is inside HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 is trivial. But changing code of all other TCP based dissectors is not...

> And then it desegments correctly. That's what other proxy dissectors (including HTTP) do. The ability to desegment needs to be restored to what it was before the proxy dissector was called.

I don't think it does.

I see few issues:

- One of client->server messages gone missing (There are three messages with "Hello 0, Websocket!" from client to server and three from server to client). Message in frame 12 is no longer dissected because it is split between frame 11 and frame 12.
- Frame 18 produces "BoundError"

> adjusts TCP tcp_dissect_pdus to deal with protocols that happen to be inside HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 streams rather than TCP

Preferably, there should be different dissectors for such a situation, and `tcp_dissect_pdus` should not get called. This looks like an unmaintainable monstrosity.

Any protocol that normally travels on TCP can be encapsulated in standard HTTP/1, HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 Connect instead of TCP. It does not really matter for HTTP/1 but matters a lot for HTTP/2 where Data travels in streams and does not correlate to outer TCP or HTTP/3 where there is no TCP layer at all.

I see two potential options for Wireshark to support dissection of TCP in HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 connect:
- modify `tcp_dissect_pdus` as suggested in this MR
- modify every single current and future dissector that normally travels on TCP to take into account potential HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 stream encapsulation instead.

It seems to me that the first approach is much easier and more manageable.

> Preferably, there should be different dissectors for such a situation, and `tcp_dissect_pdus` should not get called. This looks like an unmaintainable monstrosity.

`tcp_dissect_pdus` is called from within dissectors of protocols that normally travel on top of TCP. As far as I can tell there are 212 of them. Any of them could potentially be inside HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 CONNECT instead. Changing code of all of them seem to be a significant and risky task...

What do you recommend?

> Any of them could potentially be inside HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 CONNECT instead.

In these cases where these handles are called, aren't they all looked up from the HTTP upgrade_subdissector_table? And aren't they all required to be in the HTTP Upgrade Token Registry?

https://www.iana.org/assignments/http-upgrade-tokens/http-upgrade-tokens.xhtml

That's for Extended CONNECT. That should be a small number of dissectors, not 212.

For Plain CONNECT, it doesn't seem like it's being handled yet for HTTP2 and HTTP3 (HTTP CONNECT in `http_payload_subdissector` and other proxy dissectors call `decode_tcp_ports`). But any solution shouldn't just check for HTTP or HTTP2 or HTTP3, it needs to have the same handling for any sort of proxy dissector that currently calls `decode_tcp_ports`, such as HAPROXY.

> In these cases where these handles are called, aren't they all looked up from the HTTP upgrade_subdissector_table? And aren't they all required to be in the HTTP Upgrade Token Registry?

No, they are not. I am referring to HTTP standard CONNECT. Today Wireshark implements dissection of encapsulated protocols only inside HTTP/1 CONNECT. Enabling dissection of encapsulated protocols inside HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 CONNECT need correct de-segmentation as a pre-requisite.

There is no real difference between HTTP/1 CONNECT de-segmentation and plain TCP as HTTP/1 CONNECT does not actually have any encapsulation and application data is still directly encapsulated in TCP.

How would you recommend checking if `tcp_dissect_pdus` happens to be inside HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 without checking for specific `h2` or `h3`? Should a new flag in `pinfo` be introduced (aka `encapsulated_tcp`) or is there an existing flag that could be leveraged? Again, this check is HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 specific - there is no need to change behaviour for TCP inside HTTP/1 CONNECT. It will also become important for templated CONNECT-TCP (`draft-ietf-httpbis-connect-tcp` is nearing WGLC) for all HTTP versions.

@johnthacker I slightly changed the logic to add a `desegment_outside_tcp` boolean flag into `packet_info` structure that would be set by dissectors that call protocols normally run on top of TCP. This way `tcp_dissect_pdus` just checks that flag instead of figuring out layers and using hardcoded protocol names.
What do you think?
